summary: United Nations Security Council Resolution 129 was adopted unanimously on August 7, 1958. It called an emergency special session of the United Nations General Assembly. The resolution explained that the council's permanent members lacked unanimity at its 834th and 837th meetings, which prevented the council from carrying out its primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security.
one_line: Summary of UN Security Council Resolution 129, a unanimous 1958 measure calling an emergency special session of the General Assembly.
key_facts: United Nations Security Council resolution 129 was adopted unanimously on August 7, 1958.
Resolution 129 called an emergency special session of the General Assembly.
The resolution cited a lack of unanimity among the council's permanent members as the reason for the session.
The lack of unanimity occurred at the council's 834th and 837th meetings.
The resolution states that the lack of unanimity prevented the council from exercising its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security.
